text:
maria: Hey devex — hitting a weird parity issue between the Python SDK and our new Rust sample app for embeddings + rerank. Rust app returns vectors of length 1536, Python 2048 for the same model + input. Also the rerank endpoint returns reordered items in Rust vs Python.

devon: that's odd. Same model name, same prompt?

maria: yup. exact same model string and corpus. I printed shapes right after the SDK call. Python: `len(vec)=2048`. Rust: `len(vec)=1536`.

paul: any chance the Rust client is using a different response field or truncating? show the raw response?

maria: pasting minimal Rust snippet and raw body we get (sanitized):

```
// Rust snippet
let resp = client.embeddings().create(&request).await?;
println!("resp vectors len: {}", resp.data[0].embedding.len());
```

Raw JSON returned (trimmed): `{ "data": [{ "embedding": [0.001, 0.002, ..., <1536 values>] }], "model": "redwood-embed-xl" }`

lydia: in Python what's the call? any batching helper involved?

maria: Python call is vanilla: `client.embeddings.create(input="...", model="redwood-embed-xl")` — no batching. Rust also single call.

igor: I remember a previous change where we returned compressed/quantized vectors for the Rust path for smaller clients — but that was gated behind a header `x-rw-embed-format`. Are you sending any custom headers?

maria: nope. only auth header and content-type.

paul: the rerank ordering mismatch — is it possible the Rust SDK sorts on score vs Python preserves server order?

maria: Python returns scores [0.82,0.77,0.5] and Rust returns items in order [0.77,0.82,0.5]. same scores but shuffled.

devon: could be a map iteration change on client side when assembling results. map->vec ordering is non-deterministic in Rust unless you preserve ordering.

igor: quick ask to confirm: can you dump the full response bodies (headers + body) for both SDKs and attach? Also include `x-request-id` from response headers.

maria: attached both x-request-id values in thread. Python req id `req_py_abc123`. Rust req id `req_rs_def456`. Bodies attached below.

paul: I ran a quick correlation — `req_rs_def456` shows a server-side `302` fallback to a compact embedding variant in logs, which explains 1536 dim. Why would server pick that?

igor: that fallback should only happen when capacity/variant routing is triggered. Did your Rust client retry on 429/5xx and then resend the request without an explicit model pin? retry could cause routing to a different variant if the first host lacked capacity.

maria: ah — the Rust SDK's retry middleware is currently resending without re-attaching the `x-rw-model-version` override header we set on the original request. Python preserves it. So second try hits a different pool that serves a smaller embed variant.

devon: great find. so two issues: retry header loss -> wrong embedding variant + Rust-side collection ordering when building rerank results.

igor: filing a hotfix: (1) ensure retry clones all request headers including `x-rw-model-version` and `x-rw-embed-format` flags; (2) ensure the Rust rerank builder preserves server-provided rank order and attaches explicit scores.

sdk-ci-bot: created ticket RW-ENG-SDK-1287 for retry header preservation, assigned to @igor. link: https://rw.internal/issue/RW-ENG-SDK-1287 :raised_hands:

lydia: mark as P0 for the next patch? This will cause silent dimensional mismatch for customers bridging SDKs.

igor: agreed. also adding a regression test that compares embedding dims between Python and Rust for a canonical input and ensures response headers indicate model variant.

maria: one more small repro note for the team: if you call rerank with batching helper that builds a HashMap<id,score> then later `.into_iter()` it, ordering flips. Using Vec of tuples preserves order.

paul: leaving a short workaround in the docs: for Rust sample app, pin model with `x-rw-model-version` header and avoid HashMap when you need stable ordering. We'll patch sample app soon.

maria: thanks all — patching sample app and retesting now. will update thread when we confirm. :thumbsup:

devon: awesome, ping me if you want a quick review of the patch.

maria: updated — fixed header cloning + changed HashMap->Vec. Re-ran: both SDKs now return 2048 dims and rerank order matches. last request ids `req_rs_fix001` and `req_py_fix002`.

lydia: yay — add note to release notes under "SDK parity".

igor: PR up, will roll to canary this afternoon. thanks for the clear repro, Maria.

maria: np, that was a fun detective session :)
